title: 1:1 Quick-Prep — Focused Checkpoint for IC Growth and Delivery
content:
Purpose and constraints
- 20 minute 1:1 with Priya (senior backend eng) — keep it tight: career + top blocker + 1 concrete ask.
- Primary goal: remove one delivery blocker today and agree on next growth step (mentorship or projectlead).
- Secondary: quick check on wellbeing and calibration of workload (no deep design review here).

Agenda (20m total)
1) Quick personal check-in (2m) — mood, energy, anything time-sensitive? (ask: how was the weekend?)
2) Current sprint delivery (6m) — "what's the single biggest risk you want my help with?"
   - quick dive: reproducible failure on canary, perf regression in KV cache path
   - expected artifacts: failing test link, latest logs, PR number if blocking deploy
3) Career progression (6m) — 1 growth objective + grooming for next step
   - propose: lead an internal post-mortem + own rollout for small feature (explain scope)
   - ask: what mentoring or exposure do you need? (internal demo, cross-team design pairing)
4) Action items & checkouts (4m) — confirm owners and deadlines
5) Wrap (1m) — morale check and next 1:1 focus note

Notes to self (manager voice)
- Be explicit about timeboxing. If Priya steers into deep debugging, offer to grab logs after the meeting and schedule a 30m deep-dive later.
- Use "single biggest risk" phrasing to avoid laundry-listing.
- If she pushes back on career ask, surface concrete obstacles (time, confidence, visibility).
- Keep empathetic tone — Priya has been shipping long days last 2 sprints.

Context summary (for quick scan)
- Sprint: Q1 stable-release; Priya assigned to cache-eviction and the canary rollout.
- Known incidents: perf regression on 2028-02-03 (trace id: trace-evict-0210) — root cause suspected in memmap vs malloc path.
- Related tickets: JIRA-ENG-4823 (canary perf failures), JIRA-ENG-4760 (eviction algorithm refactor), PR #1294 (WIP, awaiting benchmark).
- Important stakeholders: infra (Arjun), platform-eng (Maya), QA (Diego).

Prep checklist (things I should pull into the meeting)
- Link to failing canary logs (cloudwatch/trace link).
- Open PR #1294 and CI screenshots.
- Short note about scope for proposed leadership task (draft 3 bullet scope).
- Quick calendar invite to pair with Arjun if performance deep-dive approved.

Hypothesis / suggested nudges to test during 1:1
- Hypothesis A: blocker is instrumentation (no visibility), so immediate unblock = attach a short reproducer + logs for Arjun.
- Hypothesis B: PR changes are fine but benchmarks were run with a different dataset; quick repro with canonical dataset likely clears the regression.
- If A or B true, offer to help: 1) schedule 45m triage with Arjun and Priya, 2) reassign a QA engineer to run canonical bench, or 3) patch quick debug metrics to canary.

Career ask framing (script)
- "Priya, I want to nominate you to lead the post-mortem and rollout plan for the eviction change — it's bite-sized ownership and will increase visibility with infra and product. You'll get my support for cross-team syncs and a co-presenter for the all-hands. Thoughts?"
- Provide alternative routes: small mentorship goal (pair with Arjun one-on-one for perf techniques) or visibility goal (lead 10-minute demo at weekly eng sync).

Potential risks and countermeasures
- Risk: Priya feels overwhelmed and declines leadership task. Counter: offer reduced scope (write the post-mortem and co-present) or postpone until next sprint.
- Risk: deep technical work eats time for career project. Counter: negotiate a 25% timebox and escalate resourcing if needed.
- Risk: perf regressions reappear in canary. Counter: temporary rollback policy and schedule full rollback plan if SLA hit threshold.

Example micro-actions to agree in meeting (templates)
- "I will DM Arjun and loop you in to schedule a 45m triage by EOD — owner: Leila, due: today 17:00."
- "You will post reproducer + failing CI link to JIRA-ENG-4823 and assign to Arjun — owner: Priya, due: today 19:00."
- "I will draft a 3 bullet scope for the post-mortem and share in Slack for feedback — owner: Leila, due: tomorrow 10:00."

Follow-up (after 1:1) — templated notes to send in Slack/Email
- Quick DM: "Thanks for the sync — I scheduled triage with Arjun at 16:30 (invite sent). Please paste the reproducer to the ticket when you have it. I'll draft the post-mortem scope by tomorrow morning."
- End-of-day update if triage yields clear next steps: post short summary to #runtime-team and tag infra/QA.

Open questions to resolve in follow-ups
- Does QA have bandwidth to run canonical benchmarks this sprint? (ask Diego)
- If not, can we carve 1 sprint of buffer or do a targeted hotfix?
- What visibility does product want for the rollout (email vs internal doc vs all-hands mention)?

Tone notes (self-reminders)
- Be curious-first, assume competence.
- Keep language concrete: timelines, owners, acceptance criteria.
- Use coaching questions rather than directives unless immediate unblocking needed.

Quick checklist before sending recap
- [ ] Confirm triage meeting scheduled and invite includes logs + PR links.
- [ ] Confirm Priya posted reproducer to ticket.
- [ ] Post short recap to Slack with next steps and owners.

Scratch/brain dump (if time runs over)
- Consider pairing Priya with a newer IC to coach test-driven perf experiments — good leadership practice without heavy scope.
- If milestone slips, propose a small customer-facing mitigation (rate-limit change) to buy time.
- Note for quarterly review: highlight ownership of post-mortem + measurable outcome (reduction in canary failures by X%).

End of doc — keep this as my working template and drop into 1:1 notes after the meeting (copy action items to calendar + ticket).
